problems.title: Multiply monomials
problems.question: Simplify5a³b·[(1/2)a⁴b⁷]³·24bc².
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: Raise each factor inside the cube to the third power; add exponents when multiplying like bases.
steps: The coefficient is 5·(1/8)·24=15. The exponents are a:3+12=15, b:1+21+1=23, c:2.

problems.title: Complete a square
problems.question: Find the minimum of x²+2x+4.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: The square is at least0, with equality at x=−1. Thus the minimum is 3.

problems.title: Median length bounds
problems.question: TriangleABC has AB=3, BC=7. Which listed value can median BM have?
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: If the two side vectors from B are u, v, then BM=|u+v|/2. Triangle inequalities give2<BM<5.
steps: The endpoints would make the triangle degenerate. Of6,2,4,1,7,5, only 4 is inside this interval.
It is attainable:the required third side from the median formula has square2·3²+2·7²−4·4²=52, which lies between4² and 10².

problems.title: Try both isosceles angle patterns
problems.question: An isosceles triangle has an exterior angle 110°. Maximise the sum of two interior angles.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: If70° is the apex, the angles are 70°,55°,55° and the largest pair sums to 125°.
If70° is a base angle, the angles are 70°,70°,40° and the largest pair sums to 140°.

problems.title: Factor a sum of odd powers
problems.question: Which listed number is the smallest multiple of 3⁷+3⁵+3³?
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: A multiple must contain prime factors 3³,7,13. Of the listed expressions, only 3³·11·7·13 contains them all.
It is 11 times the given number.

problems.title: Total degree of a product
problems.question: The degree of 19x⁴y⁴z³·9x³y^k c³ is 23. Find k.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: Total degree is the sum of all variable exponents.
steps: After multiplication it is 7+(4+k)+3+3=17+k. Set17+k=23 to getk=6.

problems.title: A difference of cubes
problems.question: Which of 15,16,17,18,20,21 divide77³−43³?
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: The value is 34·11089=377026, so it is divisible by 17.
Its last digits exclude divisibility by 20 or 16; its digit sum 25 excludes15 and 18; modulo7 it is −1, excluding21.

problems.title: Integer values allowed by triangle inequalities
problems.question: A triangle has two sides 7,12 and an integer third side. How many shapes are possible?
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: The integers 6 through18 give13 possible third sides, and each makes a nondegenerate triangle.

problems.title: A diameter gives a right angle
problems.question: O lies on BC with AO=BO=CO. If ACB=44°, find BAO.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: O is the midpoint of BC and the circumcentre, so BAC=90°.
steps: TriangleAOC is isosceles, so OAC=ACO=44°.
Therefore BAO=BAC−OAC=90°−44°=46°.

problems.title: Find a linear remainder at two roots
problems.question: Find the remainder of 2x³−9x²+14x−4 divided by x²−3x+2.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: The divisor is(x−1)(x−2); the remainder has for m R(x)=ux+v and matches the polynomial at 1,2.
steps: P(1)=3, P(2)=4. Thus u+v=3,2u+v=4, givingu=1, v=2.

problems.title: Eliminate one base using powers
problems.question: Given a³b⁷=m² and a⁵b³=m, which listed power equals a²⁶?
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: Raise the first identity to 3 and the second to 7: a⁹b²¹=m⁶, a³⁵b²¹=m⁷.
steps: For nonzero quantities, divide the second by the first to obtaina²⁶=m.
problems.note: The printed question omits a nonzero restriction. If b=0, m=0, then a is unrestricted and the requested equality need not hold; for example a=1, b=m=0.

problems.title: Expand a cube and compare coefficients
problems.question: If(2a+3b)³−16a²b−53ab²=ka³+ma²b+nab²+db³, find(k+m)/(n+d).
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: Expansion gives 8a³+36a²b+54ab²+27b³. After subtraction, the coefficients are 8,20,1,27.
The requested ratio is(8+20)/(1+27)=1.

problems.title: Identify longest and shortest sides before multiplying
problems.question: Triangle sides are 4a, a+3,2a+2; the longest times shortest is 112. Find perimeter.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: All sides positive force a>0. For a≥1, the order is a+3≤2a+2≤4a.
steps: For0<a<1, the longest-shortest product is 4a(a+3)<16, so it cannot be112.
Thus4a(a+3)=112, or(a−4)(a+7)=0. The valid parameter is 4.
The sides 16,7,10 satisfy the triangle inequality and sum to 33.

problems.title: Maximise a monomial exponent
problems.question: Find the greatest possible degree of 17x^(6n−n²)y².
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: The maximum is 11, attained at n=3, when the x-exponent is 9.

problems.title: Remainder theorem
problems.question: Find the remainder of x³−3x²+3x−3 on division by x−2.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.

problems.title: Cancel the leading terms to lower a polynomial’s degree
problems.question: For which positive integern is the degree of 9x⁷y⁶z⁵+9a⁴b³z−9x⁷y^(n−2)z⁵−9x⁷c² minimal?
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: The degree18 first term can disappear only if n−2=6.
steps: Thus n=8 makes the first and third terms cancel. The remaining terms have degrees8 and 9, so the resulting degree is 9.
For any other permissible exponent, the degree18 term remains.

problems.title: A bisector has a fixed line angle
problems.question: Triangle angles satisfy B=α, A=120°+α. Find the smaller angle between the C-bisector and AB.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: In the triangle on the B-side of the bisector, the angles at B and C sum toα+(30°−α)=30°.
The angle at the intersection with AB is 150°; its smaller line angle is 30°.

problems.title: Locate a triangle vertex from two angles
problems.question: D∈AC, AD=2, DC=1, C=45°, ADB=60°. Find A.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: Use D=(0,0), A=(−2,0), C=(1,0). Since DBC has D=120°, B lies on the ray120° from the positive horizontal axis.
steps: Write B=(−t/2,√3t/2). The 45° angle at C gives its other equation y=1−x.
Thus√3t/2=1+t/2, givingt=√3+1. The slope of AB is(3+√3)/(3−√3)=2+√3.
The exact identity tan75°=2+√3 gives A=75°.

problems.title: A remainder determines a parameter
problems.question: The remainder of x²−6x+10 divided by x−a is 1. Find a.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: Rearrange to(a−3)²=0, so a=3.

problems.title: A power sixteen times its base
problems.question: How many positive integer pairs(a, b) satisfy b=a^n=16a for a positive integern?
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: a=1 cannot work. For a>1, the possibilities are a=2, n−1=4; a=4, n−1=2; a=16, n−1=1.
They give(a, b)=(2,32),(4,64),(16,256), three pairs.

problems.title: Maximum of a downward quadratic
problems.question: The maximum of 4x−4x²+a is 5. Find a.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: The maximum is a+1, attained at x=1/2. Thus a+1=5 and a=4.

problems.title: Cancel equal power ratios
problems.question: Evaluate(12³·28⁵)/(14⁵·6³·8²).
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
steps: This is 2³·2⁵/2⁶=2²=4.

problems.title: An angle at the orthocentre
problems.question: In acute triangle ABC, the altitudes from A, C meet at M and AMC=4ABC. Find B.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: For an acute triangle, the orthocentre angle AMC=180°−B.
steps: Thus180°−B=4B, giving5B=180° and B=36°.

problems.title: A right-isosceles triangle formed by bisectors and a median
problems.question: The A- and C-bisectors and B-median for m a right-isosceles triangle. Find the original triangle’s angles.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: The smaller angle between the bisectors is 90°−B/2. It must be45°, since it cannot be90° for a nondegenerate original triangle.
steps: Hence B=90°. The median to the hypotenuse has length half the hypotenuse, so its angle with BA equals A, and its angle with BC equals C.
The median must be perpendicular to one of the two bisectors to supply the right angle. If it is perpendicular to the A-bisector, then A+A/2=90°, so A=60°, C=30°.
The other choice interchanges A, C. Thus the angle set is 30°,60°,90°.

problems.title: Exterior angles in inverse proportion
problems.question: Triangle exterior angles are inversely proportional to 22,30,33. Find largest minus smallest interior angle.
problems.idea: Simplify systematically and keep all geometric or algebraic restrictions.
formulas: $1/22:1/30:1/33=15:11:10$. The three exterior angles sum to 360°.
steps: The ratio-unit angle is 360°/36=10°. Exterior angles are 150°,110°,100°.
Interior angles are 30°,70°,80°, so the requested difference is 50°.
